name: Offers & Promotions

transitions.precondition: the offer has a code (an automatic promotion needs nothing applied and stays on the list)
transitions.provenance: ADAM CR-225 (option A), settled by Chinmay 25 October 2026: Use this offer opens the booking flow with the code, which the booking keeps (in memory, with the booking; never in storage) until WEB-010, where `applyCartPromoCode` applies it to the cart. WEB-032 has no cart and calls no cart operation.

navigation.notes: **Reached from WEB-001** — a top-level section of the site. Stated on 4 September: this screen exited somewhere and nothing exited to it, so it was outside the navigation graph entirely.

notes:
Added 17 August for parity with GST-037. **Not on the wireframe board** — needs drawing. CF-93. **`evaluatePromotions` removed 27 September 2026 (audit root R292).** It evaluates promotions against a cart — `EvaluatePromotionsRequest` requires `venueId`, `channel` and at least one line with a variant, quantity and unit price — and this screen has no cart: it arrives with `promotionId` alone. Offers apply where the cart is, on WEB-005 and WEB-010, which keep the call.

**Use this offer, the pill and the venue line (ADAM CR-225, settled by Chinmay 25 October 2026, option A; raised by Chinmay Patkar on #28185).** The client-approved frame draws all three on each card. **Use this offer** on an offer with a code opens the booking flow (WEB-002) with that code; the booking keeps it and WEB-010 applies it with `applyCartPromoCode` once the cart has a line, so this screen needs no cart. An automatic promotion needs nothing applied and stays on the list. The pill is `GuestPromotion.label` and the venue line `GuestPromotion.venues` (each `{venueId, name}`; an empty list reads *All venues*), both set in the back office. This replaces the r8 build note (ORDERS-MONEY-C11), which left the button waiting for the client.
patternReason: `listPromotions` reads the population and `getPromotion` reads one of them — list, select, act
purpose: What is on, and what applies to you.

components.label: Offers
components.provenance: decided by Chinmay, fix before Block A starts, 2 October 2026 (GFIX-3); label and venues ADAM CR-225, 25 October 2026
components.notes: The offers active now at the guest's venue, in the guest shape a guest caller receives (`GuestPromotion`). The venue is the one the guest picked on Home (`venueId` from the session, audit R267), never typed. **The card's pill is `label`** (localised, set in the back office) **and its venue line `venues`** (the names; an empty list reads *All venues*), as the client-approved frame draws them (ADAM CR-225, 25 October 2026). Was the generated table 'Every promotion'; staff and plumbing columns removed (decided by Chinmay, fix before Block A starts, 2 October 2026 (GFIX-3)).

components.label: Use this offer
components.notes: On each offer card that has a code: opens the booking flow (WEB-002) carrying the code; WEB-010 applies it with `applyCartPromoCode` once the cart has a line (ADAM CR-225, 25 October 2026). Not shown on an automatic promotion, which needs nothing applied. Drawn on the client-approved frame.
components.provenance: client-approved frame (prototype rev 3, match exact); ADAM CR-225, settled 25 October 2026

states.error: Could not load. Names which read failed and leaves the offers promotions untouched.
states.emptyFirstRun: No offers promotions yet. **Offers no create action** — this screen declares no operation that makes one — and says so rather than showing an empty table.
states.emptyNoResults: Never shown as a filter result: no offer is active at this venue now, said plainly.
states.emptyNoAccess: **There is no permission to name — a guest holds none** (ADR-0025: `x-ticvai-permission` is what a staff caller must hold; a guest call resolves to the guest's own data). No access here means one of two things, told apart by the response: not signed in, where the guest is offered sign-in and brought back to this screen, or a record that is not theirs, which says so without saying whose it is. **Never an empty table** — that reads as *there is no data* and sends somebody to support with the wrong question.
states.offline: **The offline banner shows.** What was already loaded stays on screen, marked with its age. Anything that spends money, holds capacity or changes the account waits for the connection, and its button says so rather than failing.

params.name: promotionId
params.notes: Optional (3 October 2026, CHG-SPF-004): opened without it, the screen lists them with `listPromotions` and the user picks one; an edge that holds one may still carry it to open on that record.

entryState.coldEntry: **A dead promotion link says "This offer is no longer available" and shows the list it came from** (the offers active now), with no name and no reason (r8, ORDERS-MONEY-C01; ADR-0030 as relaxed for promotions). Never a 404 page. Arrives with `promotionId`.

prototype.rev: rev 3 (pointer moved to the 30 September build, CHG-R1S-015)
prototype.differences: 'Use this offer' returns to the listing; no personalised 'applies to you' filter.

apisNote: Rebuilt 9 September 2026 from the 3 operations this screen declares, not from a workshop pack — it has none. Columns narrowed on 3 October 2026 to the fields the screen is about (CHG-SPF-002): at most five on a phone or handheld, plumbing and foreign ids left to the record itself.

offlineBanner.message: You're offline. Connect to the internet to book, pay, order or join a queue.
offlineBanner.shows: The moment the connection drops, on every screen, above the screen's own content.
offlineBanner.clears: By itself as soon as the connection is back, with a short "Back online" confirmation.
offlineBanner.never: Covers what is already on screen, or appears for a server error — that is the screen's own error state, and a guest told they are offline when the venue is down reconnects for nothing.
offlineBanner.provenance: Decided 12 September 2026 — guest web and guest app behave identically offline and say so with the same banner.

targetApp.name: TICVAI Guest
targetApp.note: **One guest product in three shells.** Web, mobile and kiosk share 73–91% of their operations; the kiosk is the same product in a fixed frame with no keyboard, and is deliberately narrower rather than different.
